- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–15% to avoid overshoot.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model should not overreact to short-term sentiment spikes.  
- If forecast is consistently overestimating true values by 5–10% over 30-day horizon, apply a 3–5% downward bias adjustment.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is rising, check for lag — if true outcome is still rising, model may be underestimating momentum.  
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a forecast peak, apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model should not overfit to recent sentiment — use 3–5 day smoothing to avoid noise-driven overreaction.
